sections.html: Around Coral Springs, sellers usually ask one thing first: spend months on the market, or take a faster deal and leave the house untouched? What the repairs would cost and how much principal remains on your loan tend to answer it. The city spreads over 24 square miles in the northwest corner of Broward County, and family buyers dominate the market.

The city counts 138,783 residents, a 3.3 percent rise since 2020. Roughly six in ten occupied homes (60.3 percent) are owner-lived, and the rest are rentals, so investor buyers are part of the competition on your street.

At $2,845 a month for a mortgaged owner, a single missed payment stings quickly, and that pressure is behind many sales.

sections.h2: How the Broward appraiser and tax collector fit in
sections.html:
Your parcel's value comes from the county appraiser, yet that office never sends the bill. A warning on its home page says a new owner is assessed at full market value, which means your own bill understates what the next owner will face.

  • Homestead filings must reach the appraiser by March 1.
  • For the 2027 roll, a late filing is accepted through September 20, 2027, with no exceptions for good cause beyond that date.
  • Sign up for the appraiser's free Owner Alert to learn when anyone records a change of ownership on your parcel.

Tax bills are issued by the tax collector, who gives 4 percent off in November and steps down to 1 percent by February.

Broward falls under the standard statewide deed rate of 70 cents per $100. Under s. 201.02 a loan secured on the property is treated as part of the price, so retiring it does not reduce the taxable amount.

  • Payment goes to the clerk at filing.
  • Each person named as a grantor stays liable for the tax.
  • The first recorded page is $5.00.

An itemized closing statement keeps any charge from surprising you.

sections.h2: Selling when you owe more than you can pay
sections.html:
Once a court enters judgment, the foreclosure auction follows in 20 to 35 days. The high bidder puts down 5 percent, and the result holds unless someone objects inside 10 days.

  • If money is left after the auction, claim it with the clerk before it is reported unclaimed.
  • A homestead owner should reach out to the clerk during that 10-day period.
  • Handing the lender a deed in lieu still triggers the deed tax.

A sale that closes before the judgment date can leave the proceeds with you.

Probate may have to come first for an inherited house. A shortened process exists under section 735.201 for modest estates, and for owners who died more than two years back.

An occupied rental adds steps. Ending a monthly tenancy takes 30 days' notice, and a demand for unpaid rent allows 3 days, leaving out weekends and court holidays. When a judge sides with the landlord, the sheriff posts a notice giving 24 hours. Should the tenant stay through the sale, spell out in writing whether the buyer inherits the lease.

1. Ask your lender for a payoff letter, and look for liens on the parcel.
  2. Check whether you hold homestead, since it ends at closing.
  3. Decide in writing who pays the November tax bill.
  4. Find two witnesses for the deed signing.
  5. Compare any offer with what an agent listing would net after repairs and fees.

Recording and ownership questions are answered on the appraiser's FAQ page or by phone at 954-357-6830. Homestead forms can go in online, by email, by fax or by mail.

Owners who have homesteaded in Coral Springs for years often sit far below market value because of the Save Our Homes cap. The state's chart prints the cap as 2.7 percent for 2026, 2.9 for 2025 and 3.0 for 2024.

None of that cap stays with the old house once it sells. A share can travel to your next Florida home through Form DR-501T, provided the new homestead starts inside a three-year window that is counted from January 1 of the year you moved out. The transfer tops out at $500,000. Amendments in chapter 2026-239 first reach the 2027 roll, so confirm the details for your case with the appraiser.

Florida offers several breaks for people still living in their homes. Every one of them ends or changes when you sell.

  • A senior whose income is under the limit may receive an extra $50,000 exemption where a local ordinance provides it. The Broward appraiser can say whether it applies.
  • A disabled ex-servicemember may get $5,000 off assessed value.
  • Form DR-570, filed by March 31, defers the part of the tax that exceeds 5 percent of income, or 3 percent for permanent residents 65 or older.

If you have a deferral, ask the collector what it means for a sale and get a payoff figure before closing. Unpaid taxes become delinquent on April 1, and a certificate can be sold against the account by June 1.

A large minority of residents, 32.1 percent, were born abroad, and 37.5 percent of people aged five and up use another language at home. Offering photos and a summary of your terms in a second language widens your audience and avoids mix-ups. Keep the translated text short and have a bilingual friend or your title agent look it over before you share it.

The city is also stable: 87.7 percent of households stayed put during the past year, so word of a sale can travel through neighbors.

County offices handle anything that touches your parcel. Completed applications can be mailed to the appraiser at 1801 NW 49 Street, Suite PA1, Fort Lauderdale, FL 33309. Staff are in on weekdays between 8 am and 5 pm. The tax collector answers at (954) 357-4829.

Storm or fire damage behind your sale? The appraiser has a catastrophic structural damage report form for a home that stayed uninhabitable for at least 30 days. When you go in person, take your deed, photo ID and newest tax bill, and jot down who helped you so a follow-up call goes smoothly. Before any buyer visit, take dated photos of the roof, kitchen, bathrooms and mechanicals, so the condition you describe matches what you can show. If a buyer's inspector later finds something you knew about, you will be glad you disclosed it early in writing.

faqs.q: What does a Coral Springs home typically cost?
faqs.a: The typical owned home is valued at $545,400 for 2020-2024. Your house may sell above or below that depending on condition and street.

faqs.q: Which county collects Coral Springs property taxes?
faqs.a: Broward County. Its appraiser sets values and its tax collector sends the bills each November.

faqs.q: What documentary stamp rate applies to a Coral Springs deed?
faqs.a: 70 cents per $100 of price, the rate that applies in every Florida county except Miami-Dade.

faqs.q: When must I file for homestead?
faqs.a: By March 1 with the appraiser, after making the house your permanent home as of January 1.

faqs.q: Can I sell if the house is in probate?
faqs.a: Only once a personal representative has authority to convey it. A deed under a probated will is listed as non-taxable.
